For this cases, the `InboundProcessingMode#CONCURRENT` should be used.
+==== Limiting the number of pending messages

+A peer that sends messages faster than the application can process them may cause an unbounded number of messages to be buffered in memory; this is especially relevant when `InboundProcessingMode#CONCURRENT` is used.
+To prevent this, Quarkus bounds the number of _pending_ (in-flight) messages, i.e. messages that a connection has received but has not yet fully processed, for a single connection.
+The limit is controlled by the following configuration property:
+When the limit is reached, the underlying WebSocket read stream is paused and no more messages are received until the pending messages are processed.
+Set the property to `0` or a negative value to disable this back-pressure completely, in which case there is no limit on the number of in-flight messages.
+Pausing the read stream also pauses the delivery of ping/pong control frames for the affected connection.
+Under sustained saturation, i.e. when the number of pending messages stays at the limit, automatic pong replies and `@OnPingMessage`/`@OnPongMessage` callbacks may be delayed.
TIP: You can choose WebSocket endpoints to which the `HttpUpgradeCheck` is applied with the `HttpUpgradeCheck#appliesTo` method.
+There is no built-in configuration property to cap the number of open connections.
+However, a stateful `HttpUpgradeCheck` can reject the HTTP upgrade once a limit is reached.
+The <<list-open-connections,`OpenConnections`>> bean provides a live snapshot of the open connections and can be consulted to count the connections of a specific endpoint.
+.Example HttpUpgradeCheck limiting the number of connections per endpoint
+<1> Only apply this check to the `foo-endpoint-id` endpoint; the `perform` method is not invoked for HTTP upgrades of other endpoints.
+<2> The endpoint id defaults to the simple name of the endpoint class but can be set with `@WebSocket#endpointId()`.
+<3> Reject the HTTP upgrade with the 503 Service Unavailable response status code once the limit is reached.
+The check runs _before_ the HTTP upgrade completes, and a connection only appears in `OpenConnections` after it has been established.
+Therefore, the snapshot returned by `OpenConnections` may not account for connections that are being established concurrently, and the limit is not strictly enforced under high concurrency.
+If you need a strict cap, maintain your own counter (e.g. an `AtomicInteger` incremented in the check and decremented in an `@OnClose` callback).
